tetel: With Christ and the Apostles General Revelation concluded.

par_cim: The Possibility of the Natural Knowledge of God in the Light of Supernatural Revelation
tetel: God, our Creator and Lord, can be known with certainty, by the natural light of reason from created things.

par_cim: The Possibility of a Proof of God’s Existence
tetel: The Existence of God can be proved by means of causality.

par_cim: God’s Existence as an Object of Faith
tetel: God’s existence is not merely an object of natural rational knowledge, but also an object of supernatural faith.

par_cim: The Natural Knowledge of the Nature of God in This World
tetel: Our natural knowledge of God in this world is not an immediate, intuitive cognition, but a mediate, abstractive knowledge, because it is attained through the knowledge of creatures.

par_cim: The Natural Knowledge of the Nature of God in This World
tetel: Our knowledge of God here below is not proper (cognitio propria) but analogical (cognitio analoga or analogica).

par_cim: The Natural Knowledge of the Nature of God in This World
tetel: God’s Nature is incomprehensible to men.

par_cim: The Supernatural Knowledge of the Divine Essence in the Other World
tetel: The blessed in Heaven possess an immediate intuitive knowledge of the Divine Essence.

par_cim: The Supernatural Knowledge of the Divine Essence in the Other World
tetel: The Immediate Vision of God transcends the natural power of cognition of the human soul, and is therefore supernatural.

par_cim: The Supernatural Knowledge of the Divine Essence in the Other World
tetel: The soul, for the Immediate Vision of God, requires the light of glory.

par_cim: The Supernatural Knowledge of the Divine Essence in the Other World
tetel: God’s Essence is also incomprehensible to the blessed in Heaven.

par_cim: The Attributes of God in General
tetel: The Divine Attributes are really identical among themselves and with the Divine Essence.
God is absolutely perfect.
God is actually infinite in every perfection.
God is absolutely simple.
There is only One God.
The One God is, in the ontological sense, The True God.
God possesses an infinite power of cognition.
God is absolute ontological Goodness in Himself and in relation to others.
God is absolute Moral Goodness or Holiness.
God is absolute Benignity.
God is absolutely immutable.
God is eternal.

par_cim: The Immensity or Immeasurability of God and His Omnipresence
tetel: God is immense or absolutely immeasurable.

par_cim: The Immensity or Immeasurability of God and His Omnipresence
tetel: God is everywhere present in created space.

par_cim: Object and Division of the Divine Knowing
tetel: The primary and formal object of the Divine Cognition is God Himself.

par_cim: Object and Division of the Divine Knowing
tetel: God knows all that is merely possible by the knowledge of simple intelligence (scientia simplicis intelligentiae).

par_cim: Object and Division of the Divine Knowing
tetel: God knows all real things in the past, the present and the future (Scientia visionis).

par_cim: Object and Division of the Divine Knowing
tetel: By the knowledge of vision (scientia visionis) God also foresees the future free acts of the rational creatures with infallible certainty.

par_cim: Object and Division of the Divine Knowing
tetel: God also knows the conditioned future free actions with infallible certainty (Scientia futuribilium).

par_cim: The Physical Properties of the Divine Will
tetel: God loves Himself of necessity, but loves and wills the creation of extra-Divine things, on the other hand, with freedom.

par_cim: The Physical Properties of the Divine Will
tetel: God is almighty.

par_cim: The Physical Properties of the Divine Will
tetel: God is the Lord of the heavens and of the earth.

par_cim: The Moral Attributes of the Divine Will
tetel: God is infinitely just.

par_cim: The Moral Attributes of the Divine Will
tetel: God is infinitely merciful.

par_cim: The Doctrinal Decisions of the Church
tetel: In God there are Three Persons, the Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost. Each of the Three Persons possesses the one (numerical) Divine Essence.

par_cim: The Internal Divine Processions in General
tetel: In God there are two Internal Divine Processions.

par_cim: The Internal Divine Processions in General
tetel: The Divine Persons, not the Divine Nature, are the subject of the Internal Divine processions (in the active and in the passive sense).

par_cim: The Procession of the Son from the Father by Way of Generation
tetel: The Second Divine Person proceeds from the First Divine Person by Generation, and therefore is related to Him as Son to a Father.

par_cim: The Procession of the Holy Ghost from the Father and the Son by way of Spiration
tetel: The Holy Ghost proceeds from the Father and from the Son as from a Single Principle through a Single Spiration.
The Three Divine Persons are in One Another.

par_cim: The Unity of the Divine Operation ad extra
tetel: All the ad extra Activities of God are common to the Three Persons.
The Father sends the Son: the Father and the Son send the Holy Ghost.

par_cim: The Mysterious Character of the Dogma of the Trinity
tetel: The Trinity of God can only be known through Divine Revelation.

par_cim: The Reality of the Divine Creation of the World
tetel: All that exists outside God was, in its whole substance, produced out of nothing by God.
The world is the work of the Divine Wisdom.

par_cim: Motive and Purpose of the Creation of the World
tetel: God was moved by His Goodness to create the world.

par_cim: Motive and Purpose of the Creation of the World
tetel: The world was created for the Glorification of God.
The Three Divine Persons are one single, common Principle of the Creation.

par_cim: Freedom of the Divine Act of Creation
tetel: God created the world free from exterior compulsion and inner necessity.

par_cim: Freedom of the Divine Act of Creation
tetel: “God was free to create this world or any other.”

par_cim: Freedom of the Divine Act of Creation
tetel: God has created a good world.

par_cim: The Temporal Character of the World
tetel: The world had a beginning in time.

par_cim: The Incommunicability of the Creative Power
tetel: God alone created the World.

par_cim: The Incommunicability of the Creative Power
tetel: No creature can, as Principal Cause (causa principalis) that is, from its own power, create something out of nothing.
God keeps all created things in existence.
God co-operates immediately in every act of His creatures.

par_cim: Divine Providence and the Government of the World
tetel: God, through His Providence, protects and guides all that He has created.

par_cim: The Origin of the First Human Pair and the Unity of the Human Race
tetel: The First Man was created by God.

par_cim: The Origin of the First Human Pair and the Unity of the Human Race
tetel: The whole human race stems from one single human pair.

par_cim: The Essential Constituent Parts of Human Nature
tetel: Man consists of two essential parts—a material body and a spiritual soul.

par_cim: The Essential Constituent Parts of Human Nature
tetel: The rational soul is per se the essential form of the body.

par_cim: The Essential Constituent Parts of Human Nature
tetel: Every human being possesses an individual soul.

par_cim: The Origin of Individual Human Souls
tetel: Every individual soul was immediately created out of nothing by God.
A creature has the capacity to receive supernatural gifts.
The Supernatural presupposes Nature.
The Supernatural perfects Nature.
God has conferred on man a supernatural Destiny.

par_cim: The Supernatural Endowment of the First Man
tetel: Our first parents, before the Fall, were endowed with sanctifying grace.

par_cim: The Supernatural Endowment of the First Man
tetel: The donum rectitudinis or integritatis in the narrower sense, i.e., the freedom from irregular desire.

par_cim: The Supernatural Endowment of the First Man
tetel: The donum immortalitatis, i.e., bodily immortality.

par_cim: The Supernatural Endowment of the First Man
tetel: The donum impassibilitatis, i.e., the freedom from suffering.

par_cim: The Supernatural Endowment of the First Man
tetel: The donum scientiae, i.e., a knowledge of natural and supernatural truths infused by God.

par_cim: The Supernatural Endowment of the First Man
tetel: Adam received sanctifying grace not merely for himself, but for all his posterity.

par_cim: The Personal Sin of Our First Parents or Original Sin
tetel: Our First Parents in Paradise sinned grievously through transgression of the Divine probationary commandment.

par_cim: The Personal Sin of Our First Parents or Original Sin
tetel: Through sin our First Parents lost sanctifying grace and provoked the anger and the indignation of God.

par_cim: The Personal Sin of Our First Parents or Original Sin
tetel: Our First Parents became subject to death and to the dominion of the Devil.
Adam’s sin is transmitted to his posterity, not by imitation, but by descent.
Original sin consists in the deprivation of grace caused by the free act of sin committed by the head of the race.
Original sin is transmitted by natural generation.
In the state of original sin man is deprived of sanctifying grace and all that this implies, as well as of the preternatural gifts of integrity.

par_cim: Existence, Origin and Number of the Angels
tetel: In the beginning of time God created spiritual essences (angels) out of nothing.
The nature of the angels is spiritual.
The angels are by nature immortal.

par_cim: The Supernatural Exaltation and Probation of the Angels
tetel: God set a supernatural final end for the angels, the immediate vision of God, and endowed them with sanctifying grace in order that they might achieve this end.

par_cim: The Supernatural Exaltation and Probation of the Angels
tetel: The angels were subjected to a moral testing,

par_cim: The fall through sin and the rejection of the bad angels
tetel: The evil spirits (demons) were created good by God; they became evil through their own fault.

par_cim: The Efficacy of the Good Angels
tetel: The primary task of the good angels is the glorification and the service of God.

par_cim: The Efficacy of the Good Angels
tetel: The secondary task of the good angels is the protection of men and care for their salvation.

par_cim: The Efficacy of the Good Angels
tetel: Every one of the faithful has his own special guardian angel from baptism.

par_cim: The Power of the Bad Angels
tetel: The Devil possesses a certain dominion over mankind by reason of Adam’s sin.

par_cim: The Dogma of the True Divinity of Christ, and Its Opponents
tetel: Jesus Christ is True God and True Son of God.

par_cim: The Reality of Christ’s Human Nature
tetel: Christ assumed a real body, not an apparent body.

par_cim: The Integrity of Christ’s Human Nature
tetel: Christ assumed not only a body but also a rational soul.

par_cim: The Adamite Origin of Christ’s Human Nature
tetel: Christ was truly generated and born of a daughter of Adam, the Virgin Mary.
The Divine and the human natures are united hypostatically in Christ, that is, joined to each other in one Person.
In the Hypostatic Union each of the two natures of Christ continues unimpaired, untransformed and unmixed with the other.

par_cim: The Duality of Wills and Modes of Operation in Christ
tetel: Each of the two natures in Christ possesses its own natural will and its own natural mode of operation.

par_cim: The Beginning and Duration of the Hypostatic Union
tetel: The Hypostatic Union of Christ’s human nature with the Divine Logos took place at the moment of conception.

par_cim: The Beginning and Duration of the Hypostatic Union
tetel: The Hypostatic Union was never interrupted.

par_cim: The Beginning and Duration of the Hypostatic Union
tetel: The Hypostatic Union will never cease.

par_cim: The Beginning and Duration of the Hypostatic Union
tetel: The Blood in the Living Body of Jesus Christ is an integral constituent part of human nature, immediately, not merely mediately, united with the Person of the Divine Logos.

par_cim: The Relationship of the Hypostatic Union to the Trinity
tetel: The Hypostatic Union was effected by the Three Divine Persons acting in common.

par_cim: The Relationship of the Hypostatic Union to the Trinity
tetel: Only the Second Divine Person became Man.

par_cim: The Natural Sonship of God of the Man Jesus Christ
tetel: Not only as God but also as man Jesus Christ is the natural Son of God.
The God-Man Jesus Christ is to be venerated with one single mode of Worship, the absolute Worship of Latria which is due to God alone.

par_cim: Adoration of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
tetel: Just as Latria is due to the whole Human Nature of Christ, so is it due to the individual parts of His nature.
Christ’s Divine and Human characteristics and activities are to be predicated of the one Word Incarnate.
The Two Natures of Christ exist in the closest union
Christ’s soul possessed the immediate vision of God from the first moment of its existence.
Christ’s human knowledge was free from positive ignorance and from error.
From the beginning of Christ’s life, His soul possessed infused knowledge (scientia infusa).

par_cim: Christ’s Acquired Knowledge and the Progress of His Human Knowledge
tetel: Christ’s soul possessed also an acquired knowledge or experimental knowledge (scientia acquisita, sc. experimentalis).
Christ was free from all sin, from original sin as well as from all personal sin.
Christ has not merely not actually sinned, but also could not sin.

par_cim: Christ’s Sanctity and Fullness of Grace
tetel: By reason of the Hypostatic Union, Christ’s human nature, through the Uncreated Holiness of the Word, is substantially Holy.

par_cim: Christ’s Sanctity and Fullness of Grace
tetel: By reason of His endowment with the fullness of created habitual grace, Christ’s soul is also accidentally holy.

par_cim: Christ’s Sanctity and Fullness of Grace
tetel: Sanctifying Grace overflows from Christ, the Head, to the Members of His Mystical Body.
Christ’s Humanity, as instrument of the Logos, possesses the power of producing supernatural effects.
Christ’s human nature was passible.
Christ’s soul was subject to sensual emotions.
The Son of God became man in order to redeem men.

par_cim: Necessity for and Freedom of the Redemption
tetel: Fallen man cannot redeem himself.

par_cim: Necessity for and Freedom of the Redemption
tetel: God was not compelled to redeem mankind by either an internal or an external compulsion.

par_cim: Necessity for and Freedom of the Redemption
tetel: Even on the presupposition of the Divine Resolve of Redemption, the Incarnation was not absolutely necessary.

par_cim: Necessity for and Freedom of the Redemption
tetel: If God demanded a full atonement the Incarnation of a Divine Person was necessary.
Christ is the Supreme Prophet promised in the Old Covenant and the absolute teacher of humanity.
The God-Man Jesus Christ is a High Priest.

par_cim: The Exercise of the Sacerdotal Office or Christ’s Sacrifice
tetel: Christ offered Himself on the Cross as a true and proper sacrifice.

par_cim: The Soteriological Importance of Christ’s Sacrifice
tetel: Christ by His Sacrifice on the Cross has ransomed us and reconciled us with God.
Christ, through His Suffering and Death rendered vicarious atonement to God for the sins of man.
Christ’s Vicarious Atonement is adequate or of full value, by reason of its intrinsic merit.
Christ’s Vicarious Atonement is superabundant, that is, the positive value of the expiation is greater than the negative value of the sin.
(i) Christ did not die for the predestined only.
(ii) Christ died not for the Faithful only, but for all mankind without exception.
Christ’s Atonement does not extend to the fallen angels.
Christ, through His Passion and Death, merited reward from God.
Christ merited for Himself the condition of exaltation (Resurrection, Transfiguration of the body, Ascension into Heaven).
Christ merited all supernatural graces received by fallen mankind.
After His Death, Christ’s soul, which was separated from His body, descended into the underworld.
On the third day after His Death Christ rose gloriously from the dead.
Christ ascended body and soul into Heaven and sits at the right hand of the Father.

par_cim: Reality of Mary’s Motherhood of God
tetel: Mary is truly the Mother of God.
Mary was conceived without stain of original sin.

par_cim: Mary’s Freedom from Evil Concupiscence and from Every Personal Sin
tetel: From her conception Mary was free from all motions of concupiscence.

par_cim: Mary’s Freedom from Evil Concupiscence and from Every Personal Sin
tetel: In consequence of a Special Privilege of Grace from God, Mary was free from every personal sin during her whole life.
Mary was a Virgin before, during and after the Birth of Jesus Christ.
Mary conceived by the Holy Ghost without the co-operation of man.
Mary bore her Son without any violation of her virginal integrity.
Also after the Birth of Jesus Mary remained a Virgin.

par_cim: The Bodily Assumption of Mary into Heaven
tetel: Mary suffered a temporal death.

par_cim: The Bodily Assumption of Mary into Heaven
tetel: Mary was assumed body and soul into Heaven.
Mary, the Mother of God, is entitled to the Cult of Hyperdulia.
Actual Grace internally and directly enlightens the understanding and strengthens the will.
There is a supernatural intervention of God in the faculties of the soul, which precedes the free act of the will.
There is a supernatural influence of God in the faculties of the soul which coincides in time with man’s free act of will.

par_cim: The Necessity of Grace for the Acts of the Supernatural Order
tetel: For every salutary act internal supernatural grace of God (gratia elevans) is absolutely necessary.

par_cim: The Necessity of Grace for the Acts of the Supernatural Order
tetel: Internal supernatural grace is absolutely necessary for the beginning of faith and of salvation.

par_cim: The Necessity of Grace for the Acts of the Supernatural Order
tetel: The justified also require actual grace for the performance of salutary acts.

par_cim: The Necessity of Grace for the Acts of the Supernatural Order
tetel: Without the special help of God the justified cannot persevere to the end in justification.

par_cim: The Necessity of Grace for the Acts of the Supernatural Order
tetel: The justified person is not able for his whole life long to avoid all sins, even venial sins, without the special privilege of the grace of God.

par_cim: Human Nature’s Capacity to Act without Grace, and the Limits of This Capacity
tetel: Even in the fallen state, man can, by his natural intellectual power, know religious and moral truths.

par_cim: Human Nature’s Capacity to Act without Grace, and the Limits of This Capacity
tetel: For the performance of a morally good action Sanctifying Grace is not required.

par_cim: Human Nature’s Capacity to Act without Grace, and the Limits of This Capacity
tetel: The Grace of Faith is not necessary for the performance of a morally good action.

par_cim: Human Nature’s Capacity to Act without Grace, and the Limits of This Capacity
tetel: Actual Grace is not necessary for the performance of a morally good action.

par_cim: Human Nature’s Capacity to Act without Grace, and the Limits of This Capacity
tetel: In the state of fallen nature it is morally impossible for man without Supernatural Revelation, to know easily, with absolute certainty and without admixture of error, all religious and moral truths of the natural order.

par_cim: Human Nature’s Capacity to Act without Grace, and the Limits of This Capacity
tetel: In the condition of fallen nature it is morally impossible for man without restoring grace (gratia sanans) to fulfil the entire moral law and to overcome all serious temptations for any considerable period of time.
Despite men’s sins God truly and earnestly desires the salvation of all men.
God gives all the just sufficient grace (gratia proxime vel remote sufficiens) for the observation of the Divine Commandments.
God gives all the faithful who are sinners sufficient grace (gratia saltem remote sufficiens) for conversion.
God gives all innocent unbelievers (infideles negativi) sufficient grace to achieve eternal salvation.
God, by His Eternal Resolve of Will, has predetermined certain men to eternal blessedness.
God, by an Eternal Resolve of His Will, predestines certain men, on account of their foreseen sins, to eternal rejection.

par_cim: The Teaching of the Church on Grace and Freedom
tetel: The Human Will remains free under the influence of efficacious grace, which is not irresistible.

par_cim: The Teaching of the Church on Grace and Freedom
tetel: There is a grace which is truly sufficient and yet remains inefficacious (gratia vere et mere sufficiens).
The sinner can and must prepare himself by the help of actual grace for the reception of the grace by which he is justified.
The justification of an adult is not possible without Faith.
Besides faith, further acts of disposition must be present.
Sanctifying Grace is a created supernatural gift really distinct from God.
Sanctifying Grace is a supernatural state of being which is infused by God, and which permanently inheres in the soul.
Sanctifying grace is not a substance, but a real accident, which inheres in the soul-substance.
Sanctifying grace is really distinct from charity.
Supernatural grace is a participation in the divine nature.

par_cim: The Formal Effects of Sanctifying Grace
tetel: Sanctifying grace sanctifies the soul.

par_cim: The Formal Effects of Sanctifying Grace
tetel: Sanctifying grace bestows supernatural beauty on the soul.

par_cim: The Formal Effects of Sanctifying Grace
tetel: Sanctifying grace makes the just man a friend of God.

par_cim: The Formal Effects of Sanctifying Grace
tetel: Sanctifying grace makes the just man a child of God and gives him a claim to the inheritance of Heaven.

par_cim: The Formal Effects of Sanctifying Grace
tetel: Sanctifying grace makes the just man a Temple of the Holy Ghost.
The three Divine or theological virtues of faith, hope and charity are infused with sanctifying grace.
The moral virtues also are infused with sanctifying grace.
The Gifts of the Holy Ghost also are infused with sanctifying grace.

par_cim: The Attributes of the State of Grace
tetel: Without special Divine Revelation no one can know with the certainty of faith, if he be in the state of grace.

par_cim: The Attributes of the State of Grace
tetel: The degree of justifying grace is not identical in all the just.

par_cim: The Attributes of the State of Grace
tetel: Grace can be increased by good works.

par_cim: The Attributes of the State of Grace
tetel: The grace by which we are justified may be lost, and is lost by every grievous sin.
By his good works the justified man really acquires a claim to supernatural reward from God.
A just man merits for himself through each good work an increase of sanctifying grace, eternal life (if he dies in a state of grace) and an increase of heavenly glory.
The Church is the Mystical Body of Jesus Christ.

par_cim: The Foundation of the Church by Christ
tetel: The Church was founded by the God-Man Jesus Christ.
Christ founded the Church in order to continue His work of redemption for all time.
By reason of her purpose and the means she uses to effect it the Church is a supernatural spiritual society.
The Church is a perfect society.

par_cim: The Hierarchical Constitution of the Church
tetel: Christ gave His Church an hierarchical constitution.

par_cim: The Hierarchical Constitution of the Church
tetel: The powers bestowed on the Apostles have descended to the bishops.
Christ appointed the Apostle Peter to be the first of all the Apostles and to be the visible Head of the whole Church, by appointing him immediately and personally to the primacy of jurisdiction.

par_cim: The Primacy of Jurisdiction of the Pope
tetel: According to Christ’s ordinance, Peter is to have successors in his Primacy over the whole Church and for all time.

par_cim: The Primacy of Jurisdiction of the Pope
tetel: The successors of Peter in the Primacy are the bishops of Rome.

par_cim: The Nature of the Papal Primacy
tetel: The Pope possesses full and supreme power of jurisdiction over the whole Church, not merely in matters of faith and morals, but also in Church discipline and in the government of the Church.

par_cim: Papal Teaching Primacy or Papal Infallibility
tetel: The Pope is infallible when he speaks ex cathedra.
By virtue of Divine right the bishops possess an ordinary power of government over their dioceses.
The individual bishop receives his pastoral power immediately from the Pope.
Christ founded the Church.
Christ is the Head of the Church.
“Our Redeemer Himself conserves with divine power the society founded by Him, the Church.” (Pius XII.)
“Christ is the Divine Redeemer of His Body, the Church.” (Pius XII.)

par_cim: The Holy Ghost and the Church
tetel: The Holy Ghost is the Soul of the Church.
The Church is indefectible, that is, she remains and will remain the Institution of Salvation, founded by Christ, until the end of the world.
In the final decision on doctrines concerning faith and morals the Church is infallible.
The primary object of the Infallibility is the formally revealed truths of Christian Doctrine concerning faith and morals.
The secondary object of the Infallibility is truths of the Christian teaching on faith and morals, which are not formally revealed, but which are closely connected with the teaching of Revelation.
The Pope is infallible when he speaks ex cathedra.
The totality of the Bishops is infallible, when they, either assembled in general council or scattered over the earth, propose a teaching of faith or morals as one to be held by all the faithful.
The Church founded by Christ is an external visible commonwealth.
The Church founded by Christ is unique and one.
The Church founded by Christ is holy.
Not only those members who are holy but the sinners also belong to the Church.
The Church founded by Christ is catholic.
The Church founded by Christ is apostolic.

The members of the Church are those who have validly received the Sacrament of Baptism and who are not separated from the unity of the confession of the Faith, and from the unity of the lawful communion of the Church.

par_cim: The Necessity for Membership of the Church
tetel: Membership of the Church is necessary for all men for salvation.

par_cim: Concept and Reality of the Communion of Saints
tetel: The members of the Kingdom of God on earth and in the other world sanctified by the redeeming grace of Christ are united in a common supernatural life with the Head of the Church and with one another.

par_cim: The Communion of the Faithful Living on Earth
tetel: By intercessory prayer the Faithful on earth can procure gifts from God for one another.

par_cim: The Communion of the Faithful Living on Earth
tetel: By good works performed in the state of grace the Faithful on earth can merit de congruo gifts from God.

par_cim: The Communion of the Faithful Living on Earth
tetel: The Faithful on earth can, by their good works performed in the state of grace, render atonement for one another.

par_cim: The Communion between the Faithful on Earth and the Saints in Heaven
tetel: It is permissible and profitable to venerate the Saints in Heaven, and to invoke their intercession.

par_cim: The Communion between the Faithful on Earth and the Saints in Heaven
tetel: It is permissible and profitable to venerate the relics of the Saints.

par_cim: The Communion between the Faithful on Earth and the Saints in Heaven
tetel: It is permissible and profitable to venerate images of the Saints.

par_cim: The Communion of the Faithful on earth and the Saints in Heaven with the Poor Souls in Purgatory
tetel: The living Faithful can come to the assistance of the Souls in Purgatory by their intercessions (suffrages).

par_cim: The Communion of the Faithful on earth and the Saints in Heaven with the Poor Souls in Purgatory
tetel: The Saints in Heaven also can come to the help of the Souls in Purgatory by their intercession.

par_cim: The Communion of the Faithful on earth and the Saints in Heaven with the Poor Souls in Purgatory
tetel: The Souls in Purgatory can intercede for other members of the Mystical Body.

par_cim: The Communion of the Faithful on earth and the Saints in Heaven with the Poor Souls in Purgatory
tetel: Suffrages are of no profit to the damned in Hell as they do not belong to the Mystical Body of Christ.
The Sacraments of the New Covenant are effective signs of grace instituted by Christ.

par_cim: The Constituent Parts of the Sacramental Sign
tetel: The outward sign of the sacraments is composed of two essential parts, namely, thing and word (res et verbum or elementum et verbum).

par_cim: The Objective Efficacy of the Sacraments
tetel: The Sacraments of the New Covenant contain the grace which they signify, and bestow it on those who do not hinder it.

par_cim: The Objective Efficacy of the Sacraments
tetel: The Sacraments work ex opere operato.
All the Sacraments of the New Covenant confer sanctifying grace on the receivers.
Each individual sacrament confers a specific sacramental grace.
Three Sacraments, Baptism, Confirmation and Holy Orders, imprint a character, that is, an indelible spiritual mark, and for this reason cannot be repeated.
The Sacramental Character is a spiritual mark imprinted on the soul.
The Sacramental Character confers the full power for the performance of acts of Christian Worship.
The Sacramental Character continues at least until the death of its bearer.

par_cim: The Institution of the Sacraments by Christ
tetel: All Sacraments of the New Covenant were instituted by Jesus Christ.

par_cim: The Institution of the Sacraments by Christ
tetel: Christ instituted all the Sacraments immediately and personally.

par_cim: The Institution of the Sacraments by Christ
tetel: Christ fixed the substance of the Sacraments. The Church has no power to alter them.
There are seven Sacraments of the New Law.
God can communicate grace even without the Sacraments.
The Sacraments of the New Covenant are necessary for the salvation of mankind.
The primary minister of the Sacraments is the God Man Jesus Christ.
The secondary minister of the Sacraments is man in the wayfaring state.
The validity and efficacy of the Sacrament is independent of the minister’s orthodoxy and state of grace.
For the valid dispensing of the Sacraments it is necessary that the minister accomplish the Sacramental Sign in the proper manner.
The minister must further have the intention at least of doing what the Church does.
Only a person in the wayfaring state can validly receive a Sacrament.
Excepting the Sacrament of Penance, neither orthodox belief nor moral worthiness is necessary for the validity of the Sacrament, on the part of the recipient.
For the validity of the Sacraments in the case of adult recipients the intention of receiving the Sacrament is necessary.
In the case of adult recipients moral worthiness is necessary for the worthy or fruitful reception of the Sacraments.

The Sacraments of Baptism, Confirmation and Consecration, when they are received validly but unworthily, revive after the removal of the moral indisposition, that is, the sacramental grace is conferred subsequently.
The Old Testament Sacraments wrought, ex opere operato, not grace, but merely an external lawful purity.

par_cim: Concept of Baptism and Its Sacramental Nature
tetel: Baptism is a true Sacrament instituted by Jesus Christ.
The materia remota of the Sacrament of Baptism is true and natural water.
The materia proxima of the Sacrament of Baptism is the ablution, by physical contact, of the body with water.
The form of Baptism consists in the words of the minister which accompany it and more closely determine it.
Baptism confers the grace of justification.
Baptism effects the remission of all punishments of sin, both the eternal and the temporal.
Even if it be unworthily received, valid Baptism imprints on the soul of the recipient an indelible spiritual mark, the Baptismal Character, and for this reason, the Sacrament cannot be repeated.
Baptism by water (Baptismus fluminis) is, since the promulgation of the Gospel, necessary for all men without exception, for salvation.
In case of emergency Baptism by water can be replaced by Baptism of desire or Baptism by blood.
Baptism can be validly administered by anyone.
Baptism can be received by any person in the wayfaring state who is not already baptised.
The Baptism of young children is valid and licit.

par_cim: Concept of Confirmation and Its Sacramental Nature
tetel: Confirmation is a true Sacrament properly so-called.
The form of Confirmation consists in the words which the minister speaks when he imposes his hands on the recipient and anoints his forehead.
As a Sacrament of the living, Confirmation effects (per se) an increase of Sanctifying Grace.
The specific operation of Confirmation is the perfection of Baptismal Grace.
Confirmation imprints on the soul an indelible spiritual mark, and for this reason, cannot be repeated.
A baptised person can achieve eternal salvation even without Confirmation.
The ordinary minister of Confirmation is the Bishop alone.
The extraordinary minister of Confirmation is a priest on whom this full power is conferred by the common law or by a special apostolic indult.
Confirmation can be received by any baptised person who is not already confirmed.
The repetition of Confirmation is invalid and grievously sinful.

par_cim: Christ’s Real Presence according to the Testimony of Holy Scripture
tetel: The Body and Blood of Jesus Christ are truly, really and substantially present in the Eucharist.
Christ becomes present in the Sacrament of the Altar by the transformation of the whole substance of the bread into His Body and of the whole substance of the wine into His Blood.
The Accidents of bread and wine continue after the change of the substance.
The Sacramental Accidents retain their physical reality after the change of the substance.
The Sacramental Accidents continue without a subject in which to inhere.
The Body and the Blood of Christ together with His Soul and His Divinity and therefore the Whole Christ are truly present in the Eucharist.
The Whole Christ is present under each of the two Species.
When either consecrated species is divided the Whole Christ is present in each part of the species.

par_cim: The Permanence of the Real Presence
tetel: After the Consecration has been completed the Body and Blood are permanently present in the Eucharist.

par_cim: The Adoration due to the Eucharist
tetel: The Worship of Adoration (latria) must be given to Christ present in the Eucharist.

par_cim: The Mysterious Character of the Eucharist
tetel: The Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist is a mystery of Faith.

par_cim: The Sacramental Nature of the Eucharist
tetel: The Eucharist is a true Sacrament instituted by Christ.

par_cim: The Outward Signs of the Eucharist
tetel: The matter for the consummation of the Eucharist is bread and wine.

par_cim: The Outward Signs of the Eucharist
tetel: The form of the Eucharist consists in Christ’s Words of institution, uttered at the Consecration.
The chief fruit of the Eucharist is an intrinsic union of the recipient with Christ.
The Eucharist, as food for the soul, preserves and increases the supernatural life of the soul.
The Eucharist is a pledge of heavenly bliss and of the future resurrection of the body.
For children before the age of reason the reception of the Eucharist is not necessary for salvation.
For adults the reception of the Eucharist is necessary for salvation with the necessity of precept (necessitate praecepti).
Communion under two forms is not necessary for any individual member of the Faithful, either by reason of Divine precept or as a means of salvation.
The power of consecration resides in a validly consecrated priest only.
The ordinary minister of the Eucharist is the priest; the extraordinary minister is the deacon (with permission of the local Ordinary or of the parish priest for some weighty reason). CIC 845.
The Sacrament of the Eucharist can be validly received by every baptised person in the wayfaring state, including young children.
For the worthy reception of the Eucharist the state of grace as well as the proper and pious disposition are necessary.

par_cim: The Sacrificial Character of the Eucharist according to the Teaching of the Church
tetel: The Holy Mass is a true and proper Sacrifice.

par_cim: The Relation of the Sacrifice of the Mass to the Sacrifice of the Cross
tetel: In the Sacrifice of the Mass, Christ’s Sacrifice on the Cross is made present, its memory is celebrated, and its saving power is applied.

par_cim: The Relation of the Sacrifice of the Mass to the Sacrifice of the Cross
tetel: In the Sacrifice of the Mass and in the Sacrifice of the Cross the Sacrificial Gift and the Primary Sacrificing Priest are identical; only the nature and mode of the offering are different.

par_cim: The Physical Nature of the Sacrifice of the Mass
tetel: The essential Sacrificial Action consists in the Transubstantiation alone.

par_cim: The Effects of the Sacrifice of the Mass
tetel: The Sacrifice of the Mass is not merely a sacrifice of praise and thanksgiving, but also a sacrifice of expiation and impetration.

par_cim: The Dogma and the Heretical Counter-propositions
tetel: The Church has received from Christ the power of remitting sins committed after Baptism.

par_cim: The Church’s Power to Forgive sins as a True Power of Absolution
tetel: By the Church’s Absolution sins are truly and immediately remitted.

par_cim: The Universality of the Church’s Power to Forgive Sins
tetel: The Church’s power to forgive sins extends to all sin without exception.

par_cim: The Judicial Character of the Church’s Power to Forgive Sins
tetel: The exercise of the Church’s power to forgive sins is a judicial act.

par_cim: The Sacramental Nature of the Church’s Forgiveness of Sins
tetel: The forgiveness of sins which takes place in the Tribunal of Penance is a true and proper Sacrament, which is distinct from the Sacrament of Baptism.
Perfect contrition bestows the grace of justification on the mortal sinner even before the actual reception of the Sacrament of Penance.
Extra-sacramental justification is effected by perfect sorrow only when it is associated with the desire for the Sacrament (votum sacramenti).
Contrition springing from the motive of fear is a morally good and supernatural act.
Imperfect contrition suffices for the forgiveness of sins in the Sacrament of Penance.

par_cim: The Divine Institution of Confession and the Necessity of Confession for Salvation
tetel: The Sacramental confession of sins is ordained by God and is necessary for salvation.
By virtue of Divine ordinance all grievous sins according to kind and number, as well as those circumstances which alter their nature, are subject to the obligation of confession.
The confession of venial sins is not necessary but is permitted and is useful.
Those sins which are already forgiven directly by the Church’s Power of the Keys are a sufficient object of confession.

par_cim: Concept and Quality of Sacramental Satisfaction
tetel: All temporal punishments for sin are not always remitted by God with the guilt of sin and the eternal punishment.

par_cim: Concept and Quality of Sacramental Satisfaction
tetel: The priest has the right and the duty, according to the nature of the sins and the ability of the penitent, to impose salutary and appropriate works of satisfaction.

par_cim: Concept and Quality of Sacramental Satisfaction
tetel: Extra-sacramental penitential works, such as the performance of voluntary penitential practices and the patient bearing of trials sent by God, possess satisfactory value.

par_cim: The Priest’s Absolution as the Form of the Sacrament of Penance
tetel: The form of the Sacrament of Penance consists in the words of Absolution.

par_cim: The Priest’s Absolution as the Form of the Sacrament of Penance
tetel: Absolution, in association with the acts of the penitent, effects the forgiveness of sins.

par_cim: The Effects of the Sacrament of Penance
tetel: The principal effect of the Sacrament of Penance is the reconciliation of the sinner with God.

par_cim: The Effects of the Sacrament of Penance
tetel: The merits due to good works performed in the state of grace which have been rendered null by grievous sins, that is, have been made inefficacious, revive.

par_cim: The Necessity of the Sacrament of Penance
tetel: The Sacrament of Penance is necessary for salvation to those who, after Baptism, fall into grievous sin.

par_cim: The Minister of the Sacrament of Penance
tetel: The sole possessors of the Church’s Power of Absolution are the bishops and priests.

par_cim: The Minister of the Sacrament of Penance
tetel: Absolution given by deacons, clerics of lower rank, and laymen is not Sacramental Absolution.

par_cim: The Recipient of the Sacrament of Penance
tetel: The Sacrament of Penance can be received by any baptised person, who, after Baptism, has committed a grievous or a venial sin.
The Church possesses the power to grant Indulgences.
The source of Indulgences is the Church’s treasury of satisfaction which consists of the superabundant satisfactions of Christ and of the Saints.
The use of Indulgences is useful and salutary to the Faithful.

par_cim: Concept and Sacramental Nature of Extreme Unction
tetel: Extreme Unction is a true and proper Sacrament instituted by Christ.

par_cim: The Outward Signs of Extreme Unction
tetel: The remote matter of Extreme Unction is oil.

par_cim: The Outward Signs of Extreme Unction
tetel: The form consists in the prayer of the priest for the sick person which accompanies the anointing.
Extreme Unction gives the sick person sanctifying grace in order to arouse and strengthen him.
Extreme Unction effects the remission of grievous sins still remaining and of venial sins.
Extreme Unction sometimes effects the restoration of bodily health, if this be of spiritual advantage.
Extreme Unction is not of itself (per se) necessary for salvation.
Only bishops and priests can validly administer Extreme Unction.
Extreme Unction can be received only by the Faithful who are seriously ill.

par_cim: Concept and Sacramental Nature of Holy Order
tetel: Holy Order is a true and proper Sacrament which was instituted by Christ.
The four Minor Orders and the Subdiaconate are not Sacraments but merely Sacramentals.
The consecration of priests is a Sacrament.
The consecration of a bishop is a Sacrament.
Bishops are superior to priests.
The Order of Diaconate is a Sacrament.

par_cim: The Outward Sign of the Sacrament of Order
tetel: The matter of the Orders of Diaconate, Priesthood, and Episcopate is the imposition of hands alone.

par_cim: The Outward Sign of the Sacrament of Order
tetel: The handing over (traditio) of the instruments is not necessary for the validity of the consecration of Deacons, Priests, and Bishops.

par_cim: The Outward Sign of the Sacrament of Order
tetel: The form of the Order of Deacon, Priest, and Bishop consists solely in the words which more closely determine the imposition of the hands.

par_cim: The Effects of the Sacrament of Holy Order
tetel: The Sacrament of Order confers sanctifying grace on the recipient.

par_cim: The Effects of the Sacrament of Holy Order
tetel: The Sacrament of Order imprints a character on the recipient.

par_cim: The Effects of the Sacrament of Holy Order
tetel: The Sacrament of Order confers a permanent spiritual power on the recipient.

par_cim: The Dispenser of the Sacrament of Order
tetel: The ordinary dispenser of all grades of Order, both the sacramental and the non-sacramental, is the validly consecrated bishop alone.

par_cim: The Dispenser of the Sacrament of Order
tetel: The extraordinary dispenser of the four Minor Orders and of the Order of Subdiaconate is the presbyter.

par_cim: The Receiver of the Sacrament of Order
tetel: The Sacrament of Order can be validly received by a baptised person of the male sex only.

par_cim: Concept, Origin and Sacramental Nature of Matrimony
tetel: Marriage was not instituted by man, but by God.

par_cim: Concept, Origin and Sacramental Nature of Matrimony
tetel: Marriage is a true and proper Sacrament instituted by God.
The primary purpose of Marriage is the generation and bringing-up of offspring. The secondary purpose is mutual help and the morally regulated satisfaction of the sex urge.
The essential properties of Marriage are unity (monogamy) and indissolubility.

par_cim: The Outward Sign of the Sacrament of Matrimony
tetel: Every valid contract of Marriage between Christians is of itself a sacrament.

par_cim: The Effects of the Sacrament of Matrimony
tetel: From the sacramental contract of marriage emerges the Bond of Marriage, which binds both marriage partners to a lifelong indivisible community of life.

par_cim: The Effects of the Sacrament of Matrimony
tetel: The Sacrament of Matrimony bestows Sanctifying Grace on the contracting parties.

par_cim: Minister and Recipient of the Sacrament of Matrimony
tetel: The contracting parties in Matrimony minister the Sacrament each to the other.
The Church possesses the sole and exclusive right to make laws and administer justice in the matrimonial affairs of baptised persons, in so far as these affect the Sacrament.
In the present order of salvation death is a punishment for sin.
All human beings subject to original sin are subject to the law of death.
With death the possibility of merit or demerit or conversion ceases.
Immediately after death the particular judgment takes place, in which, by a Divine Sentence of Judgment, the eternal fate of the deceased person is decided.
The souls of the just which in the moment of death are free from all guilt of sin and punishment for sin, enter into Heaven.

In addition to the essential bliss of Heaven which springs from the immediate Vision of God, there is also an accidental blessedness, which proceeds from the natural knowledge and love of created things.
The bliss of Heaven lasts for all eternity.
The degree of perfection of the beatific vision granted to the just is proportioned to each one’s merits.
The souls of those who die in the condition of personal grievous sin enter Hell.
The punishment of Hell lasts for all eternity.
The punishment of the damned is proportioned to each one’s guilt.
The souls of the just which, in the moment of death, are burdened with venial sins or temporal punishment due to sins, enter Purgatory.
The purifying fire will not continue after the General Judgment.
At the end of the world Christ will come again in glory to pronounce judgment.
The time of Jesus’ second coming is unknown to men.
All the dead will rise again on the last day with their bodies.
The dead will rise again with the same bodies as they had on earth.
The bodies of the just will be re-modelled and transfigured to the pattern of the risen Christ.
The bodies of the godless will rise again in incorruption and immortality, but they will not be transfigured.
Christ, on His second coming, will judge all men.
The present world will be destroyed on the Last Day.
The present world will be restored on the Last Day.
